journals.name: Nature

sources.what: "Formatting guide" — the primary Instructions for Authors: article formats, length/page budgets, order of sections, references, tables, figure legends, figures, Extended Data, Supplementary Information.

"Final submission" — production-quality specifications: fonts, figure sizing in mm, lettering point sizes, line weights, accepted electronic image formats and resolutions, RGB/CMYK, Extended Data file specs.
"Initial submission" — line numbering, file types, double-anonymized peer review option, figure resolution expectations at initial submission, cover letter.

journals.citations: IN-TEXT STYLE: numeric superscript. "References are each numbered, ordered sequentially as they appear in the text, tables, boxes, figure legends, Methods, Extended Data tables and Extended Data figure legends." "When cited in the text, reference numbers are superscript, not in brackets unless they are likely to be confused with a superscript number." Journal's own example of an in-text citation (from Final submission): "Water flows downhill 13" — with the instruction "Use superscripts for citations (see above example), not 'raised' format." "Only one publication can be listed for each number." AUTHOR TRUNCATION RULE (verbatim): "All authors should be included in reference lists unless there are more than five, in which case only the first author should be given, followed by 'et al.'." REFERENCE-LIST ENTRY PATTERN (verbatim rules): "Authors should be listed surname first, followed by a comma and initials of given names." "Titles of all cited articles are required. Titles of articles cited in reference lists should be in upright, not italic text; the first word of the title is capitalized, the title written exactly as it appears in the work cited, ending with a full stop. Book titles are italic with all main words capitalized. Journal titles are italic and abbreviated according to common usage. Volume numbers are bold. The publisher and city of publication are required for books cited." JOURNAL-ABBREVIATION POLICY: "Journal titles are italic and abbreviated according to common usage." No specific standard (ISO 4 / Index Medicus) is named. DOI POLICY: no stated requirement to supply a DOI for ordinary journal articles; datasets may be cited if they have DOIs, expressed as a full URL, with authors/title/publisher(repository name). Example dataset citation: "Hao, Z., AghaKouchak, A., Nakhjiri, N. & Farahmand, A. Global Integrated Drought Monitoring and Prediction System (GIDMaPS) data sets. figshare http://dx.doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.853801 (2014)." Preprint example: "Babichev, S. A., Ries, J. & Lvovsky, A. I. Quantum scissors... Preprint at http://arXiv.org/quant-ph/0208066 (2002)." WHAT MAY BE CITED: "Only articles that have been published or accepted by a named publication, or that have been uploaded to a recognized preprint server..., should be in the reference list; papers in preparation should be mentioned in the text." TECHNICAL: "Do not use linked fields (produced by EndNote and similar programs)." LaTeX: "Please use numerical citation styles only and ensure that the citations are numbered according to the order they appear in the text (not alphabetically)."
journals.manuscriptLimits: ARTICLES are the only research format ("Articles are the main format for original research contributions to Nature"). LENGTH IS A PAGE BUDGET, not a hard word cap: "In print, physical sciences papers do not normally exceed 6 pages on average, and biological, clinical and social-sciences papers do not normally exceed 8 pages on average. However, the final print length is at the editor's discretion." "The typical length of a 6-page article with 4 modest display items... is 2500 words... The typical length of an 8-page article with 5-6 modest display items is 4300 words." "A 'modest' display item is one that, with its legend, occupies about a quarter of a page (~270 words)." "An uninterrupted page of text contains about 1250 words." ABSTRACT ("summary paragraph"): "Articles start with a fully referenced summary paragraph, ideally of no more than 200 words, which is separate from the main text and avoids numbers, abbreviations, acronyms or measurements unless essential." Structured in substance (2-3 sentences intro; background/rationale; 'Here we show' conclusion statement; 2-3 sentences of context) but NOT formatted with section headings. TITLE: "Titles do not exceed two lines in print. This equates to 75 characters (including spaces). Titles do not normally include numbers, acronyms, abbreviations or punctuation." SUBHEADINGS: "may be up to 40 characters (including spaces)." REFERENCE CAP: "As a guideline, articles typically have no more than 50 references... Additional references for Methods or Supplementary Information are not included in this count." METHODS: "does not typically exceed 3,000 words." FIGURE LEGENDS: "fewer than 300 words each." EXTENDED DATA: "A maximum of ten Extended Data display items... is typically permitted." WHAT COUNTS: "Title, author list, acknowledgements and references are not included in total word counts." ENFORCEMENT: authors significantly over the limits "will have to shorten their papers before acceptance." NO LETTER/BRIEF-COMMUNICATION FORMAT EXISTS — the guide lists only Articles as the research format (plus Matters Arising and Corrections, whose own numeric limits live on separate pages not retrieved and are therefore not stated here). Registered Reports likewise deferred to a separate page (not stated here).
journals.requiredSections: REQUIRED ORDER (verbatim): "title, authors, affiliations (plus present addresses), bold first paragraph, main text, main references, tables, figure legends, methods (including separate data and code availability statements), methods references, acknowledgements, funding statement, author contributions, competing interest declaration, additional information (containing supplementary information line (if any) and corresponding author line), extended data figure/table legends." DATA/CODE AVAILABILITY: "Please provide separate Data Availability and Code Availability statements after the main text statements and before the Extended Data legends... Nature authors must make data and materials publicly available upon publication." AUTHOR CONTRIBUTIONS: "Authors are required to include a statement to specify the contributions of each co-author." FUNDING: "Any relevant funding information for primary research papers should be declared in a separate funding statement." ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS: "should be brief... not include thanks to anonymous referees and editors, inessential words, or effusive comments." ADDITIONAL INFORMATION (in order): Supplementary Information line (if any); Correspondence line; Peer review information (added by Nature staff); Reprints and permissions line. METHODS: "in the main text file, following the figure legends"; "subdivided by short bold headings"; "cannot contain figures or tables." REPORTING SUMMARY: required for life-sciences and behavioural/social-sciences Articles. ORCID: requested for all corresponding authors before resubmission of the final version; non-corresponding authors encouraged but not required.
journals.figureRules: COLUMN WIDTHS CONFLICT BETWEEN THE TWO OFFICIAL PAGES: Formatting guide: "Nature's standard figure sizes are 90 mm (single column) and 180 mm (double column) and the full depth of the page is 170 mm." Final submission page: "Nature's standard figure sizes are 89 mm wide (single column) and 183 mm wide (double column). The full depth of a Nature page is 247 mm. Figures can also be a column-and-a-half where necessary (120–136 mm)." Both are current, live pages — the discrepancy (esp. 170mm vs 247mm depth) is real, not resolved by the journal. FONT SIZES (verbatim, Final submission): "Separate panels in multi-part figures should each be labelled with 8 pt bold, upright (not italic) a, b, c. Maximum text size for all other text should be 7 pt; minimum text size should be 5 pt." TYPEFACE: "Lettering should be in a sans-serif typeface, preferably Helvetica or Arial." LINE WEIGHTS: "Line weights and strokes should be set between 0.25 and 1 pt at the final size." ACCEPTED FORMATS: preferred "Layered Photoshop (PSD) or TIFF format (high resolution, 300–600 dpi)" for photographic images; "Adobe Illustrator (AI), Postscript, Vector EPS or PDF format" for line drawings/graphs; fallback "JPEG (high-resolution, 300–600 dpi), CorelDraw..., Microsoft Word, Excel or PowerPoint"; explicitly rejected: "Canvas, DeltaGraph, Tex, ChemDraw, SigmaPlot." "All photographic images must be supplied at a minimum of 300 dpi." COLOUR: "Colour artwork can be provided in RGB (recommended) or CMYK format"; RGB retained online, auto-converted to CMYK for print; Nature Portfolio charges a colour-printing fee (no dollar figure stated on this page). ACCESSIBILITY: "Layering type directly over shaded or textured areas and using reversed type... should be avoided where possible." NOTE: the flagship Nature formatting/final-submission pages do NOT state a colour-blind-safe palette rule or a red/green instruction (unlike Nature Astronomy's separate branded-journals figure guide) — not stated for flagship Nature. PANEL LABELS: lowercase bold roman "a, b, c" at 8 pt in print figures; Extended Data figures use the same lowercase-letter convention. OTHER: "Lettering in figures... should be in lower-case type, with the first letter capitalized and no full stop." "Scale bars should be used rather than magnification factors." EXTENDED DATA FIGURES: RGB, max 300 ppi, file size <=10 MB, JPEG preferred (TIFF/EPS also accepted — other formats not acceptable), max page dimension 18cm x 24cm, tables at one-column (8.9cm) or two-column (18cm) width.
journals.submissionFormat: DOUBLE SPACING (verbatim): "Contributions should be double-spaced and written in English (spellings as in the Oxford English Dictionary)." LINE NUMBERS: "please include line numbers within the text"; "If providing a PDF, please number all lines. The submission system will number all lines in a Word document for you." FILE TYPES: "for initial submissions we encourage authors to present the manuscript text and figures together in a single file (Microsoft Word or PDF, up to 30 MB in size)." "Our preferred format for text is Microsoft Word, with the style tags removed." LaTeX accepted at acceptance stage; PDFs required before that. FONT: "We prefer the use of a 'standard' font, preferably 12-point Times New Roman." PAGE LAYOUT: "Separate paragraphs by a single, not a double, carriage return... Do not indent the start of paragraphs or insert page breaks at the end of sections... Do not insert a double space at the end of a sentence." Superscripts/subscripts: "apply actual super/subscript format; do not use 'raised' or 'lowered' formats." ANONYMISED REVIEW: optional, author-prepared double-anonymized review available on request. TABLES: "presented on a separate page, portrait... orientation... Tables have a short, one-line title in bold text."
journals.notes: 1) SELF-CONTRADICTION ON FIGURE DIMENSIONS between Nature's own Formatting guide (90/180mm, 170mm depth) and Final submission page (89/183mm, 247mm depth, 120-136mm column-and-a-half) — both pages are live and current; the Final submission numbers are treated as the production spec in this profile because they are the more recent/detailed production-quality page, but the conflict is real and both values are recorded rather than silently resolved. 2) NATURE HAS NO 'LETTER' OR 'BRIEF COMMUNICATION' FORMAT — only Articles, Matters Arising, and Corrections are listed; any software modelling a Nature 'Letter' type would be building a format the journal no longer runs. 3) LENGTH IS A PAGE BUDGET, NOT A HARD WORD CAP — the 2500/4300-word figures are typical lengths tied to a discipline-dependent page budget (6pg physical sciences / 8pg bio-clinical-social), with 'the final print length is at the editor's discretion'; encoded here as a single non-hard wordLimit (max 4300, the more permissive branch) with the discipline split spelled out in scope text, since the schema's WordLimit is a single number. 4) The 50-reference figure is explicitly a guideline ('As a guideline, articles typically have no more than 50 references') excluding Methods/SI references. 5) maxDisplayItems is discipline-dependent (4 for the 6-page budget, 5-6 for the 8-page budget); encoded as 6, the upper bound, with the split noted here. 6) The palette.requirement is encoded 'none-stated' for flagship Nature specifically — Nature Astronomy's sibling profile has a required Wong colorblind-safe palette from its OWN branded-journals figure guide, which does not apply to the flagship journal; this profile does not borrow it. 7) Matters Arising carries only an 18-month eligibility window on the formatting guide ('published within the past 18 months'); all its length/format limits live on a separate Matters Arising page not retrieved here, so its numeric limits are not encoded as a distinct articleType (only Article is encoded). Registered Reports are described but likewise deferred to a separate page. 8) No stageSeverity is encoded for flagship Nature: unlike Nature Astronomy (which states initial submissions need no special formatting), the flagship formatting guide does not make an equivalent statement, so no initial-submission relaxation is inferred here.

journals.name: Science (AAAS)

sources.what: Instructions for preparing an initial manuscript: manuscript format/order, title/abstract limits, figure preparation, and the full 'Science Citation Style' section with reference-list examples.
Information for authors: categories of manuscripts with word/display-item/reference limits, submission workflow, color-in-print charges.
Instructions for preparing a revised manuscript: figures as separate files, resolution requirements, accepted figure formats.
Official 'Guide to Preparing Figures' PDF (2025): file formats, resolution, fonts, line weights, RGB, colorblind-accessibility, column-width box.

journals.citations: IN-TEXT: numbered, italicized, in parentheses (NOT superscript): "(18, 19) (18–20) (18, 20–22)" — commas for collation, en dashes for ranges. Numbered in order cited through (i) main text, (ii) text boxes, (iii) figure/table captions, (iv) reference notes and acknowledgments, (v) supplementary materials; one single combined reference list covers main paper + SM. Do not use op. cit., ibid., or et al. — "Do not use ... et al. (in place of the complete list of authors' names)." Reference-list pattern: "A. B. Author, C. D. Author, Example article title. Example Journal Name 55, 100–108 (2021)." — initials first, family names in full, commas (not 'and'), full author list required, article titles included ending with a period, journal titles italic, volume bold, year in parentheses, entry ends with a period. Per-type maxReferences: Research Articles ~50 main-text; extended-format up to 100; Reviews up to 150; Analytical Reviews up to 200; Perspectives 15; Policy Forums/Articles up to 15.
journals.manuscriptLimits: Research Articles: main text up to 3000 words, abstract 125 words or less, 3-5 display items, ~50 references. Extended online format: up to 6000 words, up to 6 display items, up to 100 references. Reviews: up to 5000 words, up to 150 references, 4 display items. Analytical Reviews: up to 6000 words, up to 200 references, 4-6 display items. Perspectives: ~1000-1800 words, 15 references max, 1 display item. Titles: "no more than 96 characters (including spaces)." Abstract unstructured (no headings) with prescribed narrative flow; no citations or abbreviations in the Abstract.
journals.requiredSections: Title / Authors / Affiliations / Abstract / Main Text / References and Notes / Acknowledgments / List of Supplementary Materials / Fig. captions / Table captions (tables after references). Acknowledgments must contain, in order: contributions, Funding:, Author contributions:, [optional DEI], Competing interests:, and Data, code, and materials availability:. Single combined reference list including SM references, numbered continuously.
journals.figureRules: Widths conflict between official pages: instruction pages state 5.7/12.1/18.4 cm for 1/2/3 columns; the 2025 Guide to Preparing Figures gives a fit box of 9 cm (1 column) / 18.3 cm (2 column). Sans-serif required (Arial/Helvetica preferred); panel letters 10pt bold uppercase A, B, C; labels 6-9pt. Line weight: guide PDF states 0.28pt minimum at final print size; instruction pages state 0.5pt at final reduced size (both official, conflicting). RGB recommended; avoid red/green combinations. Minimum 300dpi raster; vector PDF/EPS/AI preferred.
journals.submissionFormat: Single spacing throughout text, tables, captions, references ("Use single spacing throughout the text, tables, figure captions, and reference list") — NOT double-spaced, unlike most other journals in this set. US letter page; Times New Roman preferred. Initial: single .docx or PDF with figures embedded, up to 30MB combined with a separate SM file. Revised: figures as separate files (PDF/EPS/AI/TIFF), no embedded figures. ORCID required for first/corresponding authors at revision.
journals.notes: Science's findings were fully researched and captured previously (docs/design/author-guidelines-findings.json, entry 'Science (AAAS)', retrieved via a real browser session since science.org blocks plain HTTP/WebFetch requests with a Cloudflare 403) and match resources/profiles/science.json exactly, field for field. This pass re-confirms that prior research rather than re-deriving it; NO correction was found, so science.json is left unchanged. Two official self-contradictions are preserved from that research: (1) column widths 5.7/12.1/18.4cm (instruction pages) vs 9/18.3cm (2025 figure-guide PDF); (2) minimum line weight 0.5pt (instruction pages) vs 0.28pt (2025 guide PDF).

journals.name: Neuron

sources.what: Neuron's main Information for Authors landing page (article types, word/figure/abstract limits).
Per-article-type word, figure, and abstract limits for Neuron (Article, Report, Resource, Perspective, etc.).
Cell Press-wide announcement: numbered superscript referencing style standard across all Cell Press journals (including Neuron) since October 2022; states the >10-author 'et al.' truncation rule.
Cell Press-wide figure guidelines (resolution tiers by image type).
Neuron 'Final File Requirements' PDF: figure resolution tiers, maximum figure dimensions.

STAR Methods guide: required Methods subsections (Resource availability incl. Data and Code Availability; Experimental Model and Study Participant Details; Method Details; Quantification and Statistical Analysis).

journals.citations: IN-TEXT: numbered superscript. Cell Press's own announcement: "Cell Press now requires all new and revised submissions [after October 2022] to format citations using the superscript numbered referencing style" (e.g. 'this observation1,2'), replacing the prior Harvard/author-year style used since Cell launched in 1974; this applies across the named list of Cell Press journals which explicitly includes Neuron. AUTHOR TRUNCATION: "'Et al.' should be used only after 10 author names" — i.e. full author list given up to 10, first-10-plus-'et al.' beyond that (confirmed independently in two separate retrievals of the same cell.com news page). No verbatim reference-list ENTRY TEMPLATE, journal-abbreviation policy, or DOI policy could be independently confirmed for Neuron specifically (Cell Press's figure-guidelines and information-for-authors pages returned HTTP 403 to every direct-fetch attempt in this session) — those fields are left null rather than reconstructed from third-party citation-style aggregators (Paperpile/EndNote/manusights.com), which were explicitly excluded as non-primary sources.
journals.manuscriptLimits: Article: total word count "under 7,000" ("including main figure legends but excluding the STAR Methods text, supplemental item legends, and references section"); Summary (abstract) "a single paragraph of 150 words or fewer"; maximum 8 figures and/or tables; graphical abstract required at 1200x1200 px. Report: "fewer than 4,000 words" (same exclusions), "no more than 4 figures and/or tables." STAR Methods itself has no character limit and is excluded from the main word count entirely.
journals.requiredSections: Title / Authors / Affiliations, Summary (Neuron's un-headed 150-word abstract), Introduction, Results, Discussion, STAR Methods (subdivided into: Resource availability [Lead Contact, Materials Availability, Data and Code Availability], Experimental Model and Study Participant Details, Method Details, Quantification and Statistical Analysis), Acknowledgments, Author Contributions, Declaration of Interests, References. Data and Code Availability is a mandatory subsection of STAR Methods' Resource availability block for every submission ("Authors must include a comprehensive and accurate data and code availability statement").
journals.figureRules: RESOLUTION TIERS (documented, Cell Press-wide): "For color or grayscale figures, at least 300 dpi is required; for black and white figures, at least 500 dpi; for line-art figures, at least 1,000 dpi at the desired print size." MAXIMUM FIGURE SIZE (Neuron Final File Requirements): "Figures should be a maximum of 6.5 x 8 in (16.5 x 20 cm) to allow for page margins and text" — this is an overall page-fit maximum, not a single/double-column preset system like Nature or Science use, so it is encoded here as maxHeightMm (20cm) with the 16.5cm width recorded in notes rather than forced into a column-preset field. Minimum/maximum font size, line-weight range, preferred font family, and colorblind-palette guidance for Neuron specifically could NOT be confirmed (cell.com/information-for-authors/figure-guidelines returned 403 on every attempt) and are left null.
journals.submissionFormat: Could not be independently confirmed for Neuron (spacing, line numbers, accepted file types) — cell.com/neuron/information-for-authors and /revise-manuscript both returned HTTP 403 on every direct-fetch attempt in this session, and no search-engine excerpt surfaced a verbatim quote precise enough to record with confidence. Left null/empty rather than assumed from sibling Cell Press journals.
journals.notes: RETRIEVAL CAVEAT (applies to this entire Neuron entry): cell.com blocks the WebFetch tool with HTTP 403 on every path attempted in this research session (information-for-authors, article-types, figure-guidelines, star-authors-guide, the STAR Methods PDF, the Final File Requirements PDF, the news page, and a web.archive.org mirror attempt which the fetch tool itself refuses to serve). Every fact above was corroborated instead through Google-indexed search-engine excerpts of those official pages — multiple independent queries returning matching, specific, institutionally-phrased numbers (e.g. the >10-author et al. rule appeared identically worded across two unrelated queries) were treated as documented; anything that surfaced only once, vaguely, or from a third-party formatting-checker blog (manusights.com, paperpile.com, scispace.com) rather than phrasing that reads as a direct quote of the official page was left null. This is a materially lower-confidence sourcing method than the direct-fetch/browser-session research behind the Nature and Science entries, and the user should independently re-verify before treating any 'documented' claim below as final.

journals.name: PNAS (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences)

sources.what: Main PNAS submission-guidelines page: article types, length/reference/figure limits, Significance Statement, format-neutral initial-submission policy.
PNAS Author Center landing page.
PNAS editorial/journal policies: data, materials, and protocol availability requirements.
PNAS 'Digital Art' figure-preparation PDF: column widths, resolution tiers by figure type, font sizes, color mode.

journals.citations: IN-TEXT: numbered, in parentheses, NOT superscript and NOT italicized (distinguishing it from Science's italic-parenthetical style): "This sentence cites one reference (1). This sentence cites two references (1, 2)." Multiple references comma-separated in one set of parentheses; ranges use an en dash, e.g. "(3-7)"; numbers assigned chronologically by first appearance in the text and reused for repeat citations. References "must be in PNAS style and numbered in the order they appear in the text." "Unpublished abstracts presented at meetings or references to 'data not shown' are not permitted." No verbatim reference-list ENTRY TEMPLATE, author-truncation threshold, journal-abbreviation policy, or DOI policy could be confirmed with primary-source confidence (pnas.org returned HTTP 403 to every direct-fetch attempt) — left null rather than reconstructed.
journals.manuscriptLimits: Research Reports: "preferred length... is 6 pages," maximum 12 pages; "a standard 6-page article is approximately 4,000 words, 50 references, and 4 medium-size graphical elements (figures and tables)." The page count "includes the title, author list, abstract, Significance Statement, main text, references, and figure legends." Abstract: "≤250 words in unstructured narrative format." Significance Statement: "maximum length is 120 words, and minimum length is 50 words" — required for all Research Reports and Stage 2 Registered Reports, written for non-specialists. Brief Reports: "limited to 3 pages, which is approximately 1,600 words... and 15 references." PNAS follows a "format-neutral policy for initial submissions" (manuscript need not match final formatting at first submission).
journals.requiredSections: Standard order: title page, abstract, introduction, results, discussion, materials and methods, acknowledgements, references, figure legends, tables — note PNAS places Results BEFORE Materials and Methods, distinct from the IMRaD-with-Methods-first convention used by most of the other journals in this set. ORCID for the corresponding author and CRediT author-contributions statement are both required; 3-6 suggested reviewers spanning each relevant discipline requested at submission.
journals.figureRules: COLUMN WIDTHS / RESOLUTION (from the Digital Art PDF, corroborated via search excerpt only — the PDF itself returned 403 to direct fetch): single column ~8.7cm, double column 10.5-18.0cm at final publication size; resolution tiers "300 dpi for halftones, 600-900 dpi for combinations, and 1000-1200 dpi for line art"; font size "≥6-8 pt at publication size"; "all fonts must be embedded in EPS and PDF files"; TIFF/EPS/high-resolution PDF only for main-text figures, TIFF saved with LZW (not JPEG) compression; "all figures should be in RGB color mode with ICC color profile embedded." Given this content could not be verified by direct primary-source read, it is recorded with a lower-confidence caveat rather than omitted (the specific, technically precise numbers — LZW vs JPEG compression, ICC profile embedding — read as genuine institutional detail unlikely to be invented by an aggregator, but independent re-verification is recommended).
journals.submissionFormat: Format-neutral at initial submission — "your manuscript does not need to adhere to strict journal formatting guidelines during initial submission." No confirmed statement on double-vs-single spacing, line numbering, or a specific accepted-file-type list at final/revised submission — left null/empty rather than assumed.
journals.notes: RETRIEVAL CAVEAT: pnas.org returned HTTP 403 to every WebFetch attempt in this session (submitting-your-manuscript, author-center, editorial-and-journal-policies, and the digitalart PDF asset), including a web.archive.org mirror attempt the fetch tool itself refused to serve. All facts above are corroborated via Google-indexed search-engine excerpts of the official pages, cross-checked across multiple independently-phrased queries for consistency (the 6-page/4000-word/50-reference/4-item figure and the 120-word Significance Statement ceiling each appeared identically across separate, unrelated queries, which is why they are marked 'documented' rather than 'inferred'). This is materially lower-confidence than a direct primary-source read; the user should re-verify before relying on any single number here for a hard compliance check.

journals.citations: Brain Stimulation uses Elsevier's Vancouver Numbered reference style (elsarticle-num citation style / "Elsevier #3 Vancouver Numbered") — a numbered, order-of-citation reference system, consistent with the broader Elsevier house convention. No verbatim in-text delimiter (brackets vs parentheses vs superscript), author-truncation threshold, journal-abbreviation policy, or reference-list entry template could be confirmed specifically for Brain Stimulation's own page (ScienceDirect and elsevier.com both returned HTTP 403 on every direct-fetch attempt) — left null rather than assumed from Elsevier's generic Vancouver convention used by other Elsevier journals, since per-journal thresholds vary across the Elsevier portfolio and borrowing one would violate the no-sibling-inference rule.
journals.manuscriptLimits: Abstract: "must not exceed 250 words" (corroborated across two independent search queries with matching wording), structured via headings covering context/background, purpose, basic procedures, and "main findings with specific effect sizes and their statistical significance"; abstracts "must be able to stand alone," avoid references and non-standard abbreviations. "Highlights" are required at submission (a short bullet-point summary, standard Elsevier requirement). Word limits for Original Articles, Brief Reports, and Letters to the Editor specifically could not be confirmed with primary-source confidence and are left null — search results returned inconsistent/unconfirmed numbers (a single weakly-sourced result suggested "5,000 words" for Original Articles and "2,000 words" for Brief Reports, but this could not be corroborated a second time from independent phrasing, so it is not encoded as documented).
journals.requiredSections: Not independently confirmed beyond the standard Elsevier structure implied by 'structured abstract' and 'Highlights' requirements. Full section order, required Data Availability / Funding / Author Contribution statement wording, and any explicit list of required sections could not be retrieved (guide-for-authors page blocked). Left null rather than assumed.
journals.figureRules: Photographs (halftones): "Color or grayscale photographs (halftones) should be saved as TIFF, JPG or PNG files using a minimum of 300 dpi" — the one figure-format fact independently corroborated. Column widths, font sizes, line weights, and colorblind/accessibility guidance for Brain Stimulation specifically could not be confirmed (the page returned 403 on every fetch attempt) and are left null rather than assumed from generic Elsevier templates, since these vary by journal.
journals.submissionFormat: Not independently confirmed (spacing, line numbers, accepted file types) — left null/empty.
journals.notes: RETRIEVAL CAVEAT: both sciencedirect.com/journal/brain-stimulation/publish/guide-for-authors and its elsevier.com redirect target returned HTTP 403 to every WebFetch attempt in this session, as did the journal's own brainstimjrnl.com domain (both the guide-for-authors deep link and the homepage, attempting to discover the guide link). This is the most sparsely-verified profile in this batch: only the citation style family (Vancouver numbered), the 250-word structured-abstract requirement, and the 300dpi TIFF/JPG/PNG photograph spec were corroborated with enough independent, consistent phrasing to record as documented. Everything else that a thorough Elsevier Guide for Authors would normally state (word limits per article type, reference-list entry template, figure column widths, line weights, required-section list, spacing/line-number policy) returned either nothing or single, unconfirmed, inconsistently-worded search results and was left null per the no-invention rule rather than filled in from Elsevier's generic house template or a sibling neuromodulation journal. The user should treat this profile as a starting skeleton requiring direct (browser-based) re-verification of the live guide-for-authors page before the word/reference/figure limits can be trusted for compliance checking.

journals.name: SLEEP

sources.what: Oxford Academic 'Author guidelines' page for SLEEP (official journal of the Sleep Research Society and American Academy of Sleep Medicine, published by Oxford University Press) — fetched directly and in full.

journals.citations: IN-TEXT: "consecutive numerical order by means of Arabic numerals placed in brackets," placed "outside periods and commas and inside colons and semicolons." "When three or more references are cited at one place in the manuscript, a hyphen should be used to join the first and last numbers of a series" (i.e. ranges collapse with a hyphen). REFERENCE STYLE: "SLEEP uses the American Medical Association 10th Edition style guide." AUTHOR TRUNCATION (verbatim): "Provide all authors' names when fewer than seven; when seven or more, list the first three and add et al." JOURNAL ABBREVIATIONS: "refer to 'List of Journals Indexed in Index Medicus'" (i.e. NLM/Index Medicus abbreviations). Sample reference (verbatim): "Lehert P, Falissard B. Multiple treatment comparison in narcolepsy: a network meta-analysis. Sleep. 2018; 41 (12). doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsy185." "Provide article titles and journal name... year, volume, issue and inclusive pages... DOIs and URLs when appropriate." PREPRINT POLICY: "SLEEP does not allow citation of preprint manuscripts in final published articles. Prior to publication of accepted papers, preprint citations must be replaced with the final, peer-reviewed version of record."
journals.manuscriptLimits: Original Articles: "There is no minimum or maximum length" (may require reduction during peer review). Review Articles: no specified word limit; systematic reviews require a PRISMA checklist. Perspectives: "should not exceed 4,000 words in length and 50 references." Research Letters: "should have 1,200 words, 10 references, one figure or table, and no abstract." Editorials: "maximum length of 1,200 words plus as many references as needed," "may include one figure or table," no section headings, maximum three authors. Worked example: "Chapman S, Trancoso R, Syktus J, Eccles R and Toombs N 2025 Impacts on compound drought heatwave events in Australia per global warming level Environ. Res. Lett. 20 054070."
